src/openms/include/OpenMS/ANALYSIS/ID/Ba.scope: Complete: AggregationMethod (product/sum/best, with maximum folding onto best) and all three run overloads - the per-run vector form, the single-run form with its own selection convention, and the consensus-map union that ignores run identifiers and optionally includes unassigned IDs. Representative selection per spectrum then per peptidoform, charge and modification collapsing, shared-peptide exclusion, PEP-to-posterior complement, nr_found_peptides annotation, minimum-peptide filtering, indistinguishable grouping and greedy peptide-centric resolution with the source's four tie-breaks. DefaultParamHandler/ProgressLogger bases become struct fields and a returned report; the SequenceToChargeToPSM pointer-map typedef is C++ plumbing with no native counterpart. Native: run identifiers and per-run accessions must be unique, score name and direction must agree within a run instead of being taken from the first ID, aggregation overflow and unreferenced Best/Mean proteins are errors rather than NaN or infinity, and every entry point commits on owned copies.

src/openms/include/OpenMS/ANALYSIS/ID/Fa.scope: The two source calculations are kept apart behind one ScoreCurve: calculate_legacy (D/T at inclusive thresholds, cumulative-minimum q-values), calculate_basic (the implemented (D+1)/(T+1) and (D+1)/(T+D+1) denominators, not the header's comments) and calculate_estimated. Ported record APIs: both apply peptide overloads including the optional peptide-level annotation, both apply protein overloads, applyEstimated, applyBasic on a PeptideIdentificationList, applyBasicPeptideLevel, applyBasic on one ProteinIdentification with groups_too, applyPickedProteinFDR with an explicit affix, and rocN over score/label pairs. split_charge_variants and treat_runs_separately build pools from observed charges and identifiers. Old scores are stored under <type>_score, output is q-value or raw FDR by option, and each mutation is transactional. PARTIAL: applyToObservationMatches over IdentificationData, all four ConsensusMap overloads (applyBasic, applyBasicPeptideLevel and both rocN), applyBasic(run_info, ids), the three applyEvaluateProteinIDs overloads and diffEstimatedEmpirical are not ported, and DecoyStringHelper::findDecoyString has no native counterpart, so picked FDR needs an explicit prefix or suffix. Unsupported variants are absent rather than stubbed.

src/openms/include/OpenMS/ANALYSIS/ID/Hy.scope: Complete: all four source overloads stay distinct because they are scientifically distinct - compute (b/y counts including cross-link $b/$y names, every matched intensity in the dot product), compute_with_detail (a/b/c prefix against x/y/z suffix counts plus mean mass error, returning the PSMDetail fields), compute_with_charges (f64 nearest peak, strict tolerance boundary, exact charge equality) and compute_with_intensity_sum (per-cleavage b/y intensity accumulated into a caller array). logfactorial_ is private in both. Native: a Tolerance value replaces the (double, bool ppm) pair; theoretical ion annotations must be present, aligned and nonempty; nonfinite or overflowing accumulations are errors instead of NaN; an invalid ion ordinal leaves the intensity array intact.

src/openms/include/OpenMS/ANALYSIS/ID/ID.scope: Only the graph operations BasicProteinInference needs are ported, and no IDBoostGraph type is exposed: connected-component partitioning of the protein/PSM bipartite graph, clusterIndistProteinsAndPeptides with annotateIndistProteins and calculateAndAnnotateIndistProteins (groups formed by identical selected-PSM neighbor sets, group score max(-1, members), ProteinGroup::sort ordering, singletons included), and resolveGraphPeptideCentric greedy razor resolution with the source's score/target/degree/accession tie-breaks and its actual PSM-node degree count. PARTIAL: the boost::variant IDPointer node model, the Graph/vertex_t/edge_t typedefs and node-set aliases, the strong typedefs PeptideCluster, Peptide, RunIndex and Charge, all six visitors (dfs_ccsplit, Label, PrintAddress, SetPosterior, GetPosterior, GetScoreTgT), both constructors, applyFunctorOnCCs and applyFunctorOnCCsST, clusterIndistProteinsAndPeptidesAndExtendGraph and its experimental-design replicate/charge hierarchy, computeConnectedComponents, getNrConnectedComponents, getComponent, getProteinIDs, printGraph, getUpstreamNodesNonRecursive, getDownstreamNodesNonRecursive and the three ScoreToTgtDecLabelPairs extractors that feed protein-level FDR are not ported. Cluster processing follows first-PSM input order where the C++ uses unordered-map iteration, so greedy output is deterministic.

Complete, under names the coverage detector does not match: both resolve overloads (keep_matching becomes ResolutionMethod::KeepMatching) as resolve_feature_map and resolve_consensus_map, both resolveAllHitRankAggregation overloads as the RankAggregation method, both resolveBetweenFeatures overloads, reduceToOnePerSpectrum as reduce_to_one_per_spectrum, and the UnresolvedIdentifications record; resolve_identifications additionally exposes the protected per-feature routine on a bare ID vector. The feature_id metadata, the 'not mapped' annotation on previously unassigned IDs, the rank-penalty formula 1 - total_rank/(max_hits*n_ids), the keep-matching overload's retention of all sorted hits on the winner, and the source sequence-length-first key ordering are preserved. Native: populated competing IDs must agree on score type and direction rather than trusting the first record, empty IDs cannot win selection (avoiding the source's unchecked hit dereference), modification identity replaces C++ residue-modification pointer ordering, the report adds an inconsistent_score_type counter, and each map mutation commits only after the whole operation succeeds.

Complete: rip partitions borrowed protein/peptide slices into owned RippedFile copies covering all three origin conventions (file_origin, map_index, id_merge_index), the split_ident_runs and numeric_filenames flags, every RipFileIdentifier field (run index, origin index, origin_fullname and the extension-stripped output_basename), and detectOriginAnnotationFormat_ as the public detect_origin_annotation_format. The two C++ rip overloads collapse into one result whose files already carry the RipFileIdentifierIdxComparator order; IdentificationRuns and the RipFileMap typedef are construction plumbing with no native counterpart, and UNKNOWN_OAF is rejected at detection rather than represented as a value. Native: nothing is opened or written and neither input is mutated, a protein accession resolves within its own run (the C++ global table lets a later run overwrite another run's sequence and scores), a numeric origin index may not denote different paths across runs without run splitting, and empty or accession-less IDs are returned as skipped_peptide_identifications instead of being silently dropped. Both protein-group vectors are omitted from output copies, as copyMetaDataOnly does, and counted.

src/openms/include/OpenMS/ANALYSIS/ID/Mo.scope: Complete: both compute overloads and every Result field (matches, n_peaks, score, MIC, TIC, err, err_ppm) as MorpheusResult. The source's two separate ordered traversals are preserved, so the counted-theoretical and summed-experimental passes can disagree; so is its division of both error sums by the theoretical match count, the inclusive tolerance boundary, the ppm window relative to theoretical m/z, the 1e10 error sentinel when nothing matched, the all-zero result for an empty spectrum, and f32 result precision after f64 accumulation. The charge-aware overload requires exact charge equality including zero and does not search past a mismatch. Native: a Tolerance value replaces the (double, bool ppm) pair; zero total experimental intensity, a matched theoretical m/z of zero, mismatched charge-array lengths, unsorted or negative input and overflow are errors instead of NaN.

src/openms/include/OpenMS/ANALYSIS/ID/Pe.scope: Ported: the in-memory run overload, which rewrites peptide evidence and target/decoy labels and rebuilds protein hits per run; the Unmatched and MissingDecoy policies in full; decoy prefix/suffix rules including the source DecoyHelper inference and its DECOY_ fallback, with resolve_decoy_rule returning the getDecoyString/isPrefix pair; IL_equivalent with protein-side J folding; the aaa_max and mm_max budgets with protein-side-only ambiguity expansion; auto enzyme and specificity resolution from each run's search parameters; the second/third-residue N-terminal exception and Asp|Pro adventitious cleavage; write_protein_sequence, write_protein_description and keep_unreferenced_proteins. A returned IndexingReport replaces the logged target/decoy and unique-match statistics. PARTIAL: only the vector overload exists - the two FASTAContainer<TFI_File> and <TFI_Vector> streaming overloads, the AUTO_MODE constant, the ExitCodes enum (errors are Result), the names_of_unmatched and names_of_missing_decoy string tables, and the DefaultParamHandler/ProgressLogger bases with their threads option are not ported. Matching is a bounded scalar matcher with a per-peptide cache carrying the same ambiguity and mismatch semantics, not the source Aho-Corasick trie; proteome-scale throughput parity is explicitly not claimed.

src/openms/include/OpenMS/ANALYSIS/ID/Pr.scope: Complete: all five public statics and every PurityScores field. computePrecursorPurity is compute (inclusive isolation and tolerance boundaries, doubled tolerance in the source's ppm operation order, charge sign ignored and charge zero read as one, isotopes matchable without the monoisotopic peak, residual interfering spectrum retained); computePrecursorPurities is compute_all, keyed by MS2 native ID with the source's referenced-or-most-recent parent lookup and the ignore_missing_precursor_spectra flag; computeSingleScanPrecursorPurities and computeInterpolatedPrecursorPurity are compute_single_scan and compute_interpolated, which deliberately keep their separate fuzzy binary32 conventions, half weights and unclipped ratios; countSPSPrecursorsMatchingPeptideFragments is count_sps_matches, counting duplicate windows independently against binary32-narrowed b/y bounds. combinePrecursorPurities is private in both. Native: a Tolerance value replaces the (double, bool ppm) pair, inputs are validated for sorted finite nonnegative peaks and never modified, invalid or duplicate MS2 native IDs and missing parents are errors instead of a warning plus an empty map, and a 100,000-scan and 50-million-unit work budget bounds the traversal. The header's claim that scores are combined over the previous and next MS1 is stale relative to its own implementation; the port follows the code.

src/openms/include/OpenMS/ANALYSIS/MAPMA.scope: Ported: four of the five transformRetentionTimes overloads - PeakMap (every spectrum RT and every chromatogram sample), FeatureMap (centroids, stored hull outline vertices, subordinates, assigned and unassigned peptide IDs), ConsensusMap (centroids without recomputing from handles, every source handle, assigned and unassigned IDs) and a peptide-identification slice - plus the protected applyToFeature_ and applyToConsensusFeature_ as public single-record methods, and storeOriginalRT_'s write-once original_RT rule. The source's choice not to transform spectrum-attached identification RTs is the default, with an explicit opt-in flag. Hull outlines are transformed vertex-wise without rebuilding the convex hull, as in the source, which converts a scan-envelope hull into an outline-only hull. PARTIAL: transformRetentionTimes(IdentificationData&) is not ported, since no IdentificationData adapter exists in this module. Native: each container is prepared and committed atomically so a failure in the last chromatogram sample or unassigned ID leaves everything unchanged, and chromatogram original times are stored under the source's lower-case original_rt key as a decimal string because spectrum metadata is still a string map.

Ported: the anchor store kept separate from the fitted model, construction from DataPoints, setDataPoints (which resets the model to none), fitModel, apply plus a batch apply_values, getDataPoints, getModelType via TransformationModel::name, invert and a non-mutating inverse (both refit swapped anchors, as the source does, and are therefore approximate), getDeviations, getStatistics with the source's fixed 100/99/95/90/75/50/25 percentile selections and discrete rank formula, and estimateWindow with the full adaptive rule - interpolated quantile, Tukey Q3+1.5*IQR winsorized robust estimate, and the tail-density blend from 1 to 10 percent with its fallback for fewer than four residuals or zero IQR. PARTIAL: the static getModelTypes name list, printSummary and getModelParameters (a Param object; the port carries a typed ModelConfig instead) are not ported, and of the six advertised model types only none, identity, linear, interpolated and lowess can be fitted - b-spline is absent, and no natural-spline approximation is offered in its place.

Ported: the DataPoint value in full - x, y and note, construction from a coordinate pair, and the source's tuple ordering and equality via derived PartialOrd/PartialEq - and the identity base behavior as TransformationModel::None and ::Identity, whose evaluate passes the coordinate through. The coordinate 'weights', which the source names misleadingly and which are coordinate transforms rather than per-observation regression weights, become a CoordinateWeight of a WeightFunction (identity, ln, 1/|x|, 1/x^2) plus min/max bounds: weightDatum is transform, unWeightDatum is untransform, and checkDatumRange's clamping is folded into transform_training, which - following the source - clamps only for a nonidentity function and never clamps at evaluation. PARTIAL: the entire Param-based surface is absent - getParameters, the static getDefaultParameters and checkValidWeight's string validation have no counterpart, and getValidXWeights/getValidYWeights are replaced by the closed WeightFunction enum. The batch weightData/unWeightData helpers are not exposed. The port is a closed enum of models rather than a virtual base with derived classes, so there is no polymorphic TransformationModel to subclass.

Ported as InterpolatedModel: construction from anchors, which sorts them and averages y at repeated x and requires at least three distinct x values even for linear interpolation, as the source does; evaluate as apply; and all three extrapolation policies - two-point-linear (the default, one chord through the first and last averaged anchor), four-point-linear and global-linear least squares over every original anchor including repeated x. Cubic interpolation uses the native CubicSpline2d natural boundary conditions. PARTIAL: of the three interpolation types only linear and cspline exist - akima is not implemented, and no other spline is presented in its place. The Param constructor overloads and the static getDefaultParameters are absent (a typed InterpolationOptions replaces them), and the public abstract Interpolator class has no counterpart because the port uses a closed enum rather than a pluggable interpolator.

Complete as LinearModel: the data-fitted constructor is fit (one anchor gives slope one and the observed offset, two anchors their exact line, three or more centered covariance over variance) and the explicit-parameter constructor is from_coefficients, which - as in the source - applies only when no anchors are supplied; evaluate is apply; the eight-output getParameters is coefficients() for slope/intercept plus options() for both weight functions and their datum bounds; invert is inverse(), using the reciprocal slope with the adjusted intercept, exchanging the x and y weight configurations, and rejecting a zero slope; getDefaultParameters becomes LinearOptions::default. The symmetric_regression flag is deliberately absent: the pinned C++ assigns it but never uses it, so the port exposes the ordinary fit it actually performs rather than an ineffective switch.

src/openms/include/OpenMS/ANALYSIS/OPENS.scope: Both data structs are ported in full because MRMFeature stores one by value and IDScoresAsMetaValue takes the other: OpenSwath_Scores becomes OpenSwathScores with the source's field names and every per-field default, including the five that start at -1 to mark 'not computed' rather than 0, and OpenSwath_Ind_Scores becomes OpenSwathIndScores with ind_num_transitions, ind_transition_names and all 40 per-transition vectors, which the port - like the source - does not require to agree in length. A native KEY_SUFFIXES list names the 42 metadata suffixes the source writes. PARTIAL: the struct's four scoring methods (get_quick_lda_score, calculate_lda_prescore, calculate_lda_single_transition, calculate_swath_lda_prescore) are not ported - their bodies live in OpenSwathScores.cpp and belong to the OpenSWATH analysis work package - and OpenSwath_Scores_Usage's 20 boolean switches are not ported either, being an analysis-side switchboard no ported header touches. This entry records the data model; it does not claim the scoring header.

Ported: all three operations over both containers - integratePeak, estimateBackground and calculatePeakShapeMetrics for MSChromatogram and MSSpectrum - and all three result structs complete, PeakArea (area, height, apex_pos and the selected hull points), PeakBackground and every one of PeakShapeMetrics' 16 fields, with the source's sampled, uninterpolated threshold positions, its zero tailing/asymmetry factor when the apex coincides with the sampled start, its f32 baseline slope that is not divided by width, and its baseline-delta-to-height ratio. All three integration types (intensity_sum, trapezoid, and nonuniform Simpson with its even-count averaging that can reach a sample outside the bounds) and all four baseline constants are typed enums whose names round-trip, with vertical_division parsed as the min form it names. Optional EmgGradientDescent preprocessing integrates the fitted span, as the source EMGPreProcess_ does. PARTIAL: six of the twelve entry points are absent - the ConstIterator-bound overload of each operation for each container has no counterpart, since the port takes positions - and getDefaultParameters with the DefaultParamHandler Param surface is not ported. Native: a 1,000,000-point ceiling is checked before validation or allocation, inputs and their annotations are never modified, and nonfinite results are errors while the source's finite negative areas are retained.

Complete: one pick_chromatogram returns what both source overloads produce - the picked chromatogram and the smoothed trace - and its picked record carries the five FLOATINDICES arrays in source order and under the source names (FWHM, IntegratedIntensity, leftWidth, rightWidth, SN), with SN filled with -1 unless report_sn is set or signal_to_noise exceeds zero. Both native methods are ported: legacy finds boundaries on the raw signal, corrected on the smoothed one while integrating raw intensities. Gaussian and Savitzky-Golay smoothing (including the source's increment of an even frame length), PeakPickerHiRes seeding at its own fixed S/N 1 and 200 s noise window independent of the boundary settings, peak_width boundary extension, the median noise estimator at the source's 1000 s window, and overlapping-peak removal all follow the pinned implementation. The Crawdad path is deliberately absent: it is a WITH_CRAWDAD-conditional wrapper around an external library, and neither native method is presented as reproducing it. Native: a PickingCompatibility switch names the exact source behaviours (duplicate retention times, negative intensities) the default refuses, boundary indices into the original sampling replace the f32-rounded leftWidth/rightWidth metadata for callers that need full precision, and the picker never modifies its input.

src/openms/include/OpenMS/ANALYSIS/XLMS/.scope: Complete ProteinProteinCrossLink value and reaction enum only. Arc allocation identity supplies source pointer equality/hash with owned lifetimes; finite private linker mass and normalized signed-zero hash. Defaults, position/terminal/name/correction fields and cross/loop/mono selection retained. Other OPXL records and comparators remain unimplemented; no whole-header completion or C++ hash-byte equivalence claimed.

Only the post-processing tail is ported, as private helpers of the mzIdentML reader, because readMzIdentMLFile's cross-linking path is not meaningful without them: addProteinPositionMetaValues (add_protein_position_meta_values, whose residue numbering corrects the C++ reader's unconverted one-based start), addBetaAccessions, addXLTargetDecoyMV (add_crosslink_target_decoy), removeBetaPeptideHits (merge_crosslink_hits), computeDeltaScores and addPercolatorFeatureList with its PERCOLATOR_FEATURES list - six of the header's fifteen distinct operations, run in the source's order. PARTIAL: the entire search algorithm is unported - enumerateCrossLinksAndMasses, digestDatabase, buildCandidates, collectPrecursorCandidates, filterPrecursorsByTags, buildFragmentAnnotations, buildPeptideIDs, combineTopRanksFromPairs, computePrecursorError, isoPeakMeans and the PeptideIDScoreComparator predicates - and none of the ported six is public API. The sibling value type is covered separately by the OPXLDataStructs.h entry (src/chemistry/protein_cross_link.rs); the cross-link ladders live in src/chemistry/theoretical_xlms.rs.

src/openms/include/OpenMS/CHEMISTRY/AAIn.scope: Every public member: the four residue classifiers aliphatic/acidic/basic/polar, all ten AAindex tables (KHAG800101, VASM830103, NADH010106, NADH010107, WILM950102, ROBB760107, OOBM850104, FAUJ880111, FINA770101, ARGP820102) and calculateGB with its 500 K default. Native: the ten tables are the AAIndexScale enum with accession() and value() instead of ten static getters; ALL preserves the source declaration order. Unknown or lowercase codes are errors, not the source's exception-or-sentinel mix, and calculate_gb returns Result. The protected GBsidechain_/GBleft_/GBdeltaright_ tables back calculate_gb and are private, as they are in the source.

src/openms/include/OpenMS/CHEMISTRY/AASe.scope: The modified peptide value: fromString as parse/FromStr (round-bracket names, UniMod accessions and square-bracket absolute or delta masses, with the source's decimal-count precision rule for resolving a numeric tag to a registry record), toString as Display, toUniModString, empty, size, isModified, getFormula/getAverageWeight/getMonoWeight over the full Residue::ResidueType surface as formula_for/average_mass_for/mono_mass_for, getPrefix/getSuffix/getSubsequence, every setModification/setNTerminalModification/setCTerminalModification form including the mass-tag variants and registry-aware versions, both terminal-modification accessors and their names, equality and operator< as Ord. PARTIAL: toUnmodifiedString, toBracketString, getAAFrequencies, has(const Residue&), hasSubsequence, hasPrefix, hasSuffix, both operator+ and operator+= concatenations, operator[] and getResidue (residue access is crate-private; only the unmodified text is public through as_str), the Iterator/ConstIterator classes, operator>>, the permissive fromString flag that maps stop codons to X, and std::hash are not ported. getMZ is mz(charge) for the full peptide only, without the ResidueType argument. Native: masses and formulas return Result, since B/Z/X and numeric mass tags have no invented composition; negative charges divide by the absolute charge; parsing and formula work are bounded.

src/openms/include/OpenMS/CHEMISTRY/Addu.scope: Every public member: the component constructor with its mol_multiplier default and all three invariants, parseAdductString, getNeutralMass, getMZ, getMassShift with the average-weight switch, isCompatible, getCharge, getName, getEmpiricalFormula, getMolMultiplier and the four-field operator==. Native: fields are immutable after checked construction, the conversions return Result instead of throwing, and parsing is bounded by MAX_ADDUCT_TEXT_BYTES/MAX_ADDUCT_TERMS/MAX_ADDUCT_WORK.

src/openms/include/OpenMS/CHEMISTRY/Cros.scope: Both public members: getInstance as CrossLinksDB::global(), which loads the shipped XLMOD.obo cross-linker terms, and getAllSearchModifications as all_search_modifications(), listing the entries that carry a PSI-MOD accession. The public ModificationsDB inheritance is reached through database()/database_mut(), and from_obo builds a caller-owned cross-link registry from any XLMOD stream. Native: composition instead of inheritance, and the private makeCrossLinkProviders_ becomes the cross_links_only flag of OboReadOptions.

src/openms/include/OpenMS/CHEMISTRY/Deco.scope: Every public member: the default constructor and setSeed (with_seed/set_seed over the source's seeded Mersenne-Twister stream), reverseProtein, reversePeptides, shuffle with its decoy_factor default, and shufflePeptides with the source's identity-driven retry loop and its cross-protein decoy cache. The private SequenceIdentity_ ratio and the source's shuffle conventions are reproduced. Native: the protease is the Protease enum rather than a name string (Protease::from_name accepts the source spellings, including "no cleavage"), results are Result values, and input, output, variant, cache and work sizes are bounded.

src/openms/include/OpenMS/CHEMISTRY/Dige.scope: The CRTP registry surface, realized twice rather than as a generic base: ProteaseDB and RNaseDB each provide getInstance as global(), getEnzyme (case-insensitive by name and synonym), getAllNames as names(), hasEnzyme(name), hasRegEx, and beginEnzyme/endEnzyme as the enzymes() slice. PARTIAL: hasEnzyme(const DigestionEnzymeType*) has no equivalent, and the protected registration machinery addEnzyme_/loadFromProviders_ is absent because both registries are compiled and immutable, so there is no DigestionEnzymeDataProvider. Native: getEnzymeByRegEx is ProteaseDB::enzymes_by_regex, which returns every enzyme carrying that expression instead of the source's single arbitrary winner; lookups return Result rather than throwing ElementNotFound/IllegalArgument.

The protease metadata record for all 33 pinned enzymes: name, regular expression and its description, synonyms, getNTermGain and getCTermGain as parsed EmpiricalFormula values with the source H/OH defaults, and the search-engine identifiers getPSIID, getXTandemID, getCometID, getMSGFID and getOMSSAID. PARTIAL: the record is a compiled immutable table, so the public constructors, all seven setters (setNTermGain, setCTermGain, setPSIID, setXTandemID, setCometID, setMSGFID, setOMSSAID) and the file-driven setValueFromFile override are not ported; neither are operator< , the regular-expression comparison operators operator==/operator!=(const std::string&) or operator<<. Native: the numeric engine identifiers are Option<i32> so the source's -1 'absent' sentinel is explicit, and metadata is reached through the Protease enum.

Both cleavage-code expressions and both terminal gains: getCutsAfterRegEx, getCutsBeforeRegEx, getFivePrimeGain and getThreePrimeGain, for all 14 pinned RNases. The four setters are the public fields of DigestionEnzymeRNARecord, which from_record validates and freezes, so an enzyme is built rather than mutated in place. setValueFromFile is absent for the stated reason that RNA enzyme XML import is outside this increment (docs/CHEMISTRY_SUPPORT.md). Native: RNA fields take part in value identity, unlike the inherited C++ equality, and records are ordered and hashable.

src/openms/include/OpenMS/CHEMISTRY/Elem.scope: The immutable element value: name, symbol, atomic number, the isotope table, and getMonoWeight/getAverageWeight as mono_mass/average_mass computed from that table. PARTIAL: the element is a validated read-only record obtained from element()/element_table(), so the public constructors and all six setters (setAtomicNumber, setAverageWeight, setMonoWeight, setIsotopeDistribution, setName, setSymbol) are not ported, and neither are operator<, operator<< or the std::hash specialization. getIsotopeDistribution has no IsotopeDistribution-returning form; isotopes() returns the tabulated masses and abundances as a slice. Native: private fields keep the nonempty-isotope-table invariant across copies, and the OPENMS_CHEMISTRY_ELEMENT_*_DEFAULT sentinels have no place because there is no default-constructed element.

All 84 declared element tables with their isotope masses and abundances, reached through element_table() and the name-or-symbol lookup element(); iridium uses the declared iridium table rather than the rhenium tables the pinned source passes to buildElement_ (CPP-249). PARTIAL: getElement(unsigned int) and both hasElement overloads are not ported, and the three accessor maps getNames/getSymbols/getAtomicNumbers have no equivalent. Native: a compiled static table replaces the getInstance singleton and its protected build/clear machinery; the database is immutable, so no registration API is offered.

src/openms/include/OpenMS/CHEMISTRY/Empi.scope: Parsing (including (13)C labels, D/T aliases, negative counts and signed terminal charge), toString as Display, getMonoWeight, getAverageWeight, getCharge/setCharge as charge/with_charge, getNumberOfAtoms, getNumberOf by element symbol, isEmpty, contains, equality, and operator+/-/* as checked_add/checked_sub/checked_scale that error on i32 overflow instead of wrapping. The three estimateFrom* members are ported onto AveragineComposition as estimate_average_mass, estimate_mono_mass and estimate_average_mass_with_sulfur, which return a FormulaEstimate carrying the formula and the source's success flag. getIsotopeDistribution and getConditionalFragmentIsotopeDist are inverted onto the generators (CoarseIsotopePatternGenerator::run and calc_fragment_isotope_dist). PARTIAL: getLightestIsotopeWeight (the lightest_mass helper is private), calculateTheoreticalIsotopesNumber, addChargeAdduct, toMap, isCharged, hasElement, the static hydrogen()/water() constructors, the element-map iterators (begin/end), operator< and std::hash are not ported. Native: charge means protons added or removed, as in the source; mz() rejects a negative calculated mass and zero charge.

src/openms/include/OpenMS/CHEMISTRY/Enzy.scope: The shared digestion base, carried on ProteaseDigestion rather than a separate type: getMissedCleavages/setMissedCleavages and getSpecificity/setSpecificity as fields, getEnzymeName/setEnzyme, getSpecificityByName as FromStr for DigestionSpecificity, both digestUnmodified overloads as digest_unmodified (string slices) and digest_ranges (start/past-the-end pairs), isValidProduct as is_valid_product_unmodified, and countInternalCleavageSites. SPEC_NONE, SPEC_SEMI and SPEC_FULL are DigestionSpecificity::None/Semi/Full. PARTIAL: filterByMissedCleavages is not ported; the Specificity values SPEC_UNKNOWN, SPEC_NOCTERM and SPEC_NONTERM (the last two unsupported in the source class itself) and the NamesOfSpecificity table have no equivalent. The NoCleavage and UnspecificCleavage name constants appear only as Protease enum variants. Native: the digest functions return the products instead of the source's count of length-discarded products, inclusive length bounds use None for an unbounded maximum, and generation is bounded by max_products/max_work.

src/openms/include/OpenMS/CHEMISTRY/Hydr.scope: All four public members: computeGRAVY, computeProfile, computeWindowedProfile and computeHydrophobicMoment, with the source window-size (7 and 11) and angle (100 degrees) defaults and the clamp when the window exceeds the sequence. All seven scales of the HydrophobicityScaleMethod enum are tabulated without reorientation or normalization. Native: associated functions rather than const methods on a stateless class; empty sequences, zero windows and the six sentinel codes B/J/O/U/X/Z return errors instead of throwing.

src/openms/include/OpenMS/CHEMISTRY/ISOT.scope: run, convolve, convolvePow_, calcFragmentIsotopeDist, the peptide/RNA/DNA and composition estimators, isotope overrides and the mass mode (native conventions in docs/ISOTOPE_SUPPORT.md). ProbabilityPrecision::SourceSingle reproduces the source's binary32 Peak1D arithmetic: bit-identical to the executed SDK runs that iterate elements in the port's order (ascending atomic number for natural elements; 198 of 200 runs for CHNOPS, because the SDK's pointer-keyed element map changes order between runs), except formulas containing iridium, which the SDK builds from rhenium's tables. Class-test literals are tier 3. PARTIAL: setMaxIsotope, setRoundMasses, getIsotopeOverrides and estimateForFragmentFromPeptideWeightAndS are not ported. Native: f64 by default; the abundance override with the stray (0, 1) peak is rejected; errors replace infinities and NaN, including when every binary32 bin underflows (the crate-private estimate_from_peptide_weight_source reports that case to FeatureFinderAlgorithmPicked, which empties the window as the source's NaN weights do).

src/openms/include/OpenMS/CONCEPT/HashUt.scope: Three of the header's six inline functions are ported bit-exactly, and they are ported twice, privately, rather than as a shared CONCEPT module. src/param/value.rs carries fnv1a_hash_bytes as `fnv` (offset basis 14695981039346656037, prime 1099511628211, wrapping multiply), hash_combine as `combine` with the same seed ^= value + 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15 + (seed << 6) + (seed >> 2) recurrence, and hash_float as `hash_float`, including the header's `if (value == T(0)) value = T(0)` signed-zero normalisation; ParamValue::source_hash64 exposes the composed result and tests/param_value.rs pins literal expected values (for example -0.0 hashing to 0xe4ab8baccf524eae) that were written as explicit little-endian bytes rather than generated from the port. src/format/controlled_vocabulary.rs::fnv1a_hash is fnv1a_hash_string over a &str, public and documented as 'Source FNV-1a byte hash, explicitly 64-bit on every target' -- which also fixes the source's std::size_t width, so a 32-bit C++ host would disagree with both. Every other native type reaches hashing through std::hash::Hash with the caller's Hasher (docs/METADATA_HASH_SUPPORT.md lists the fields each one visits and repeats the -0 normalisation), so those hash values are NOT the header's FNV-1a values; no observable output or file format depends on them. PARTIAL: (1) hash_int<T> and hash_char have no counterpart -- callers spell out fnv(&x.to_le_bytes()) instead, which additionally fixes the endianness the source leaves native; (2) hash_float is f64-only, while the source template also covers float and long double; (3) both ports are private to their module or to a format module, so nothing in concept:: offers these helpers and a third caller would port them a third time; (4) there is no CONCEPT/HashUtils module at all, which is why the detector could only match this header through provenance manifests.
